05-01-2020 "Just want to point out a few things based on statements presented.

The below image that was snipped from post #6606 in this thread regarding the Lebron James card in question.
serf21 was the owner of the card when it was graded as a BGS 8 by Beckett.
In his post to an unnamed forum from November of 2006 he claims that he had sent it twice to Beckett and each time the card was graded a BGS 8.

So to clarify, according to the one-time owner in his own words, the card (while he owned it) was twice graded by experts at Beckett and each time the card was given the grade of BGS 8.
In the same post #6606 of this thread, another forum member in November of 2006 described the actual auction and included the Ebay auction link where the seller (serf21) sold
the card and noted in the listing that "The card is in near-mint condition with slight chipping on the bottom left corner".

Subsequently the card was sold by serf21 with the noted chipping to the lower left corner.
The same card resurfaced on Ebay in November of 2006 and the grade had improved to a BGS 9.5 with no mention of chipping
or visible chipping to the bottom left corner and the auction was ended without a sale (according to the 2006 forum post)." https://www.blowoutforums.com/showpost.php?p=15832504&postcount=6705

"This copy sold raw on eBay on August 6, 2006 for $11.2k. Unfortunately, Worthpoint does not go past November 2006, but I was able to locate an image of the card from that auction. It is not obvious that there is any corner damage." https://www.blowoutforums.com/showpost.php?p=15603607&postcount=3950 

03-01-2020 "Now, let us examine the "evidence" of trimming proposed by these members. The photograph shown of the card in it's un-graded state points out the bottom left & right corner with notes (the bottom right corner note states, "Debris in scan goes off card") which is alarming in and of itself.

If anyone here is familiar with photo editing or photoshopping, you would know that absolutely ANYTHING & or EVERYTHING can be done to a photograph showing what the editor wants the viewer to see, to include adding lines that would indicate corner damage which is non existen; however in this case the editor of the photograph extended his line beyond the card itself (amateur mistake or oversight) not sure which but it is convincing enough to me and many others that this line was artificially added.

Something to think about:

IF this significant corner damage previously existed & the card was indeed trimmed, the spacing from the bottom of the text "2003-04 EXQUISITE COLLECTION" and the bottom edge of the card would be so significant, it would be absolutely impossible for the card to meet the dimensions published by Upper Deck for this product." https://www.blowoutforums.com/showpost.php?p=15604728&postcount=3951

Won this in @goldinco a few months ago but just now getting into my possession after 1. Paying down the purchase via consignment 2. Getting it regraded by PSA

This card was originally “authentic” and while some may consider it more valuable than crossing it to a psa 6, I prefer knowing the actual numeric grade for a card of this stature (for lower end cards I’m perfectly fine with “Authentic” and an auto grade)

Grader notes explain there is a crease near the top right of the patch and to me that ok - for cards with really nice patches there is often inevitable border damage.

This card fits into my “personal iconic 100 card collection” as it gets Steph into that case in a high end way AND is great representation for the National Treasures brand.

It’s the first year of NT and I like the fact the patch is from the jersey in the photo. It’s a bit of a tip of the cap to the 2003 exquisite lebron which is a photo shoot jersey patch.

While some may argue that the /99 is more iconic than this /25 version but for me personally what matters most is the quality of the signature and quality of the patch

11/21/2023 Patch authenticity disputed. An earlier image reportedly shows 44/99 with a plain white patch, while the current BGS 9 card contains a multicolor patch. Upper Deck issued a 2019 letter concluding that the card was authentic and describing it as a factory replacement for a damaged original. Federal court records later noted that the letter authenticated the card but did not expressly authenticate the embedded patch. Goldin Auctions withdrew the card from a June 2021 auction after bidding reached $690,000 because of authenticity concerns. The owners subsequently sued Goldin. The litigation remains centered on Goldin’s decision to withdraw the card and conflicting interpretations of Upper Deck’s records; no court ruling located has determined that the patch was either authentic or altered. https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCOURTS-njd-1_23-cv-01202/pdf/USCOURTS-njd-1_23-cv-01202-0.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com

FYI, 64/99 may also have been doctored for a significant dent in the back of the card. Just doing more research on these and it's crazy how far back the alterations go. There's someone I need to reach out to in an attempt to get a picture of it as the one that was posted online is no longer available at its original URL, or has been deleted from the hosting service entirely.

The significance here is that 64/99 which is a botched alteration has a 9.5 on the surface, but if this dent was doctored, then that means it's nowhere near a 9.5 for that sub grade, which I would assume brings the overall grade down below a 6 and the perceived value with it.

4/20/19 Go to this thread (Page 6, https://www.blowoutforums.com/showth...=828012&page=6) and read from post 135 to post 142. (Make sure you look at the dates too.)
Now, consider that this card was originally a BGS 9 (as revealed in the thread linked above) and then became a BGS 6. I wonder how that might have happened? Obviously someone cracked it out, the centering and surface didn't change much, but the corners and edges were obliterated. I've cracked cards out of slabs before so that I could put them in mags, but the process of cracking a card out of a slab would not cause the condition to change unless you clip the card itself or you deliberately cause damage to the edges and corners. (Edges and corners are number one when it comes to trim jobs.) https://www.blowoutforums.com/showpost.php?p=14591693&postcount=3671

This is easily Albert's most controversial 2001 issue. In 2001, Fleer placed clear, peel off stickers on 300 of the regular Fleer Legacy cards. Collectors could choose to either peel the sticker off and keep the unsigned card or send it in and receive an autographed version once Albert got around to signing them. Once the redemptions were filled, these were very hot. However, around the time of Fleer's bankruptcy, there was a deluge of them listed on eBay. It is important to note, however, many of these are FAKE and FORGERIES. It is very easy for the trained eye to distinguish between the different cards. 

https://collectingpujols.blogspot.com/search/label/2001%20Fleer%20Legacy
The authentic versions have a compact signature in the middle, lower portion of the card while the fakes contain a large, looping signature closer to the middle of the card.

https://forums.collectors.com/discussion/630465/alert-fake-pujols-fleer-legacy-rookie-autos-scans

https://www.blowoutforums.com/showthread.php?t=1102889&highlight=2001+Pujols+Legacy+auto

https://www.net54baseball.com/showthread.php?t=235686
I know that there are fake 2001 Fleer Legacy Pujols autos. This happened due to the way the exchange program worked combined with Fleer going out of business and selling blank (non signed) cards in auction.

From my research it looks like the authentic ones should be limited to the first 300 and that his auto should be lower and smaller on the card. 

https://x.com/tiffanycards/status/1815835768142909644
Only the first 300 serial numbers were autographed. Any cards serial numbered above 300 should not feature an autograph.

BEWARE OF FAKES!!

Check out these website for more info:

https://collectingpujols.blogspot.com/2009/08/2001-fleer-legacy.html
This is easily Albert's most controversial 2001 issue. In 2001, Fleer placed clear, peel off stickers on 300 of the regular Fleer Legacy cards. Collectors could choose to either peel the sticker off and keep the unsigned card or send it in and receive an autographed version once Albert got around to signing them. Once the redemptions were filled, these were very hot. However, around the time of Fleer's bankruptcy, there was a deluge of them listed on eBay. It is important to note, however, many of these are FAKE and FORGERIES. It is very easy for the trained eye to distinguish between the different cards. 

https://collectingpujols.blogspot.com/search/label/2001%20Fleer%20Legacy
The authentic versions have a compact signature in the middle, lower portion of the card while the fakes contain a large, looping signature closer to the middle of the card.

https://forums.collectors.com/discussion/630465/alert-fake-pujols-fleer-legacy-rookie-autos-scans

https://www.blowoutforums.com/showthread.php?t=1102889&highlight=2001+Pujols+Legacy+auto

https://www.net54baseball.com/showthread.php?t=235686
I know that there are fake 2001 Fleer Legacy Pujols autos. This happened due to the way the exchange program worked combined with Fleer going out of business and selling blank (non signed) cards in auction.

From my research it looks like the authentic ones should be limited to the first 300 and that his auto should be lower and smaller on the card. 

https://x.com/tiffanycards/status/1815835768142909644
Only the first 300 serial numbers were autographed. Any cards serial numbered above 300 should not feature an autograph.

This is easily Albert's most controversial 2001 issue. In 2001, Fleer placed clear, peel off stickers on 300 of the regular Fleer Legacy cards. Collectors could choose to either peel the sticker off and keep the unsigned card or send it in and receive an autographed version once Albert got around to signing them. Once the redemptions were filled, these were very hot. However, around the time of Fleer's bankruptcy, there was a deluge of them listed on eBay. It is important to note, however, many of these are FAKE and FORGERIES. It is very easy for the trained eye to distinguish between the different cards. 

https://collectingpujols.blogspot.com/search/label/2001%20Fleer%20Legacy
The authentic versions have a compact signature in the middle, lower portion of the card while the fakes contain a large, looping signature closer to the middle of the card.

https://forums.collectors.com/discussion/630465/alert-fake-pujols-fleer-legacy-rookie-autos-scans

https://www.blowoutforums.com/showthread.php?t=1102889&highlight=2001+Pujols+Legacy+auto

https://www.net54baseball.com/showthread.php?t=235686
I know that there are fake 2001 Fleer Legacy Pujols autos. This happened due to the way the exchange program worked combined with Fleer going out of business and selling blank (non signed) cards in auction.

From my research it looks like the authentic ones should be limited to the first 300 and that his auto should be lower and smaller on the card. 

https://x.com/tiffanycards/status/1815835768142909644
Only the first 300 serial numbers were autographed. Any cards serial numbered above 300 should not feature an autograph.

https://collectingpujols.blogspot.com/2009/08/2001-fleer-legacy.html
This is easily Albert's most controversial 2001 issue. In 2001, Fleer placed clear, peel off stickers on 300 of the regular Fleer Legacy cards. Collectors could choose to either peel the sticker off and keep the unsigned card or send it in and receive an autographed version once Albert got around to signing them. Once the redemptions were filled, these were very hot. However, around the time of Fleer's bankruptcy, there was a deluge of them listed on eBay. It is important to note, however, many of these are FAKE and FORGERIES. It is very easy for the trained eye to distinguish between the different cards. 

https://collectingpujols.blogspot.com/search/label/2001%20Fleer%20Legacy
The authentic versions have a compact signature in the middle, lower portion of the card while the fakes contain a large, looping signature closer to the middle of the card.

https://forums.collectors.com/discussion/630465/alert-fake-pujols-fleer-legacy-rookie-autos-scans

https://www.blowoutforums.com/showthread.php?t=1102889&highlight=2001+Pujols+Legacy+auto

https://www.net54baseball.com/showthread.php?t=235686
I know that there are fake 2001 Fleer Legacy Pujols autos. This happened due to the way the exchange program worked combined with Fleer going out of business and selling blank (non signed) cards in auction.

From my research it looks like the authentic ones should be limited to the first 300 and that his auto should be lower and smaller on the card. 

https://x.com/tiffanycards/status/1815835768142909644
Only the first 300 serial numbers were autographed. Any cards serial numbered above 300 should not feature an autograph.

This is easily Albert's most controversial 2001 issue. In 2001, Fleer placed clear, peel off stickers on 300 of the regular Fleer Legacy cards. Collectors could choose to either peel the sticker off and keep the unsigned card or send it in and receive an autographed version once Albert got around to signing them. Once the redemptions were filled, these were very hot. However, around the time of Fleer's bankruptcy, there was a deluge of them listed on eBay. It is important to note, however, many of these are FAKE and FORGERIES. It is very easy for the trained eye to distinguish between the different cards. 

https://collectingpujols.blogspot.com/search/label/2001%20Fleer%20Legacy
The authentic versions have a compact signature in the middle, lower portion of the card while the fakes contain a large, looping signature closer to the middle of the card.

https://forums.collectors.com/discussion/630465/alert-fake-pujols-fleer-legacy-rookie-autos-scans

https://www.blowoutforums.com/showthread.php?t=1102889&highlight=2001+Pujols+Legacy+auto

https://www.net54baseball.com/showthread.php?t=235686
I know that there are fake 2001 Fleer Legacy Pujols autos. This happened due to the way the exchange program worked combined with Fleer going out of business and selling blank (non signed) cards in auction.

From my research it looks like the authentic ones should be limited to the first 300 and that his auto should be lower and smaller on the card. 

https://x.com/tiffanycards/status/1815835768142909644
Only the first 300 serial numbers were autographed. Any cards serial numbered above 300 should not feature an autograph.

Collectors could choose to either peel the sticker off and keep the unsigned card or send it in and receive an autographed version once Albert got around to signing them. Once the redemptions were filled, these were very hot. However, around the time of Fleer's bankruptcy, there was a deluge of them listed on eBay. It is important to note, however, many of these are FAKE and FORGERIES. It is very easy for the trained eye to distinguish between the different cards. 

https://collectingpujols.blogspot.com/search/label/2001%20Fleer%20Legacy
The authentic versions have a compact signature in the middle, lower portion of the card while the fakes contain a large, looping signature closer to the middle of the card.

https://forums.collectors.com/discussion/630465/alert-fake-pujols-fleer-legacy-rookie-autos-scans

https://www.blowoutforums.com/showthread.php?t=1102889&highlight=2001+Pujols+Legacy+auto

https://www.net54baseball.com/showthread.php?t=235686
I know that there are fake 2001 Fleer Legacy Pujols autos. This happened due to the way the exchange program worked combined with Fleer going out of business and selling blank (non signed) cards in auction.

From my research it looks like the authentic ones should be limited to the first 300 and that his auto should be lower and smaller on the card. 

https://x.com/tiffanycards/status/1815835768142909644
Only the first 300 serial numbers were autographed. Any cards serial numbered above 300 should not feature an autograph.

Base /799, Auto /799

BEWARE OF FAKES!!

Check out these website for more info:

https://collectingpujols.blogspot.com/2009/08/2001-fleer-legacy.html
This is easily Albert's most controversial 2001 issue. In 2001, Fleer placed clear, peel off stickers on 300 of the regular Fleer Legacy cards. Collectors could choose to either peel the sticker off and keep the unsigned card or send it in and receive an autographed version once Albert got around to signing them. Once the redemptions were filled, these were very hot. However, around the time of Fleer's bankruptcy, there was a deluge of them listed on eBay. It is important to note, however, many of these are FAKE and FORGERIES. It is very easy for the trained eye to distinguish between the different cards. 

https://collectingpujols.blogspot.com/search/label/2001%20Fleer%20Legacy
The authentic versions have a compact signature in the middle, lower portion of the card while the fakes contain a large, looping signature closer to the middle of the card.

https://forums.collectors.com/discussion/630465/alert-fake-pujols-fleer-legacy-rookie-autos-scans

https://www.blowoutforums.com/showthread.php?t=1102889&highlight=2001+Pujols+Legacy+auto

https://www.net54baseball.com/showthread.php?t=235686
I know that there are fake 2001 Fleer Legacy Pujols autos. This happened due to the way the exchange program worked combined with Fleer going out of business and selling blank (non signed) cards in auction.

From my research it looks like the authentic ones should be limited to the first 300 and that his auto should be lower and smaller on the card. 

https://x.com/tiffanycards/status/1815835768142909644
Only the first 300 serial numbers were autographed. Any cards serial numbered above 300 should not feature an autograph.
